name: Mezo USD
oneLiner: MUSD is Mezo's BTC-only overcollateralized stablecoin on Mezo's Bitcoin L2, minted at 110% minimum against native and wrapped BTC via Liquity v1.
pegMechanism: BTC-only overcollateralized CDP with direct $1 BTC redemption; operates on Mezo (Bitcoin L2, not Ethereum or a Stage 1 L2)

oracleRisk.summary: Mezo MUSD uses one BTC collateral path whose PriceFeed reads a single Chainlink-compatible BTC/USD oracle, rejects data older than 60 seconds, and supplies the price to Liquity-style trove liquidation.

branchApplicability.rationale: MUSD is issued from BTC-backed borrower troves with a 110% minimum collateral ratio. Mezo's published contracts use one shared PriceFeed, TroveManager, StabilityPool, and redistribution engine for that BTC collateral path, so one complete branch row covers the liquidation surface.

branches.label: Mezo BTC troves
branches.summary: All MUSD troves use the shared Mezo PriceFeed BTC/USD answer to calculate individual collateral ratios and liquidation eligibility.

feeds.provider: Mezo PriceFeed with Chainlink-compatible Skip Connect BTC/USD oracle
feeds.path: Skip Connect BTC/USD answer -> Mezo PriceFeed.fetchPrice -> TroveManager ICR

branches.fallbackBehavior: PriceFeed.fetchPrice reverts when the configured oracle answer is more than 60 seconds old or the oracle call fails. The contract has no secondary source or stored last-good-price fallback; the owner can replace the configured oracle through setOracle.

collateralParameters.note: A trove becomes liquidatable when its individual collateral ratio falls below the fixed 110% MCR.

branches.liquidationMechanism: Any caller may submit one or more active troves for immediate liquidation. TroveManager first offsets principal and interest against MUSD in the StabilityPool, transfers proportional BTC collateral to the pool, and redistributes any uncovered debt and collateral to remaining active troves.
branches.backstop: The MUSD StabilityPool is the first-loss backstop and is seeded by protocol-controlled value; StabilityPool deposits burn against liquidated debt and receive the seized BTC collateral.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Debt exceeding available StabilityPool MUSD is redistributed with its remaining collateral across active troves through the DefaultPool reward indices. A stale or failing oracle halts price-dependent liquidation by reverting, and the reviewed contracts do not implement a last-good-price or global shutdown settlement path.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Mezo documents the MUSD bridge between Mezo, Ethereum, and Base using Wormhole NTT. Because cross-chain supply relies on Wormhole NTT bridge contracts, the reviewed route is external lock/mint.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The exact MUSD source and Ethereum ABI show that addToBurnList(address) is onlyOwner and burn(account, amount) checks only burnList[msg.sender], then burns the specified account without that account's approval or allowance. At Ethereum block 25534618, Base block 48643892, and Mezo block 10403815, owner() returned 0x98D8899c3030741925BE630C710A98B57F397C7a and burnList(owner) returned false on all three deployments; their 6,436-byte runtime layouts differ only in a 34-byte chain-specific range. The current owner can therefore grant arbitrary-account burn ability on each deployment. transfer and transferFrom have no separate blacklist or pause check, but this owner-grantable burn path is direct individual holder impairment.

reserves.name: Bitcoin (BTC) — native and wrapped variants (tBTC, WBTC, SolvBTC, cbBTC)

sources.label: Mezo MUSD liquidation and redemption mechanics

reserveReview.rationale: Mezo documents MUSD as a Bitcoin-collateralized CDP. Borrowed MUSD is backed by BTC placed in the ActivePool; collateral returns on repayment, is paid out on redemptions, or moves to the StabilityPool or DefaultPool following liquidation. The documented design is BTC-only, so no unsupported multi-asset allocation is asserted.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Mezo MUSD collateral, custody, liquidation, and redemption documentation
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The published product documentation does not disclose a current split among native BTC and supported wrapped-BTC variants.
